correctness.rationale: TARGET route (research_report.claim_route=TARGET). Verified independently: (1) Enumeration: replay.py fresh reverse-order backtrack regenerates 3441 normalized orthomorphisms, matching OEIS A003111 (11*3441=37851) and run_all.py forward enumeration; auditor re-ran replay.py -> REPLAY_OK. (2) Canonical reduction: all 363 seeds satisfy theta(0)=0, theta|_{1..10} and psi(d)=theta(d)-d permutations of 1..10; each equals its 10-multiplier orbit minimum under theta^a(d)=a*theta(a^-1 d); pairwise non-isomorphic; completeness (orbit-min set equals archived set) checked; orbit-size distribution 10^336 5^12 2^6 1^9 sums to 3360+60+12+9=3441. Auditor re-verified all clauses. (3) Transversal counts: count_log_A and count_log_B agree on all 363 seeds (hashes match DRAFT); replay third-method reverse-row bitmask spot recounts pass; auditor additionally recounted one seed per spectrum value with independent fixed-row bitmask code: 3333,3443,3476,3553,3597,3795,3949,4389,4411,37851 all match with multiplicities 33,33,66,66,9,36,66,36,9,9 summing to 363. (4) Maximum: 9 maximizers are exactly the 9 linear maps theta(d)=c*d c=2..10 (c=1 correctly absent since psi=0); S_max=[0,2,4,6,8,10,1,3,5,7,9] (c=2) orbit-minimum; count 37851 matches Wanless DB LS11mosttrans and A006717. (5) Mates: universal mate M(i,j)=j-i proof checked analytically (M Latin; (L,M)=(u,v) gives d=v,i=u-theta(v),j=i+v unique; each T_m={(i,i+m)} has distinct rows/cols/symbols theta(m)+i); pair-enumeration verified for all 363 in replay; auditor validated all 363 mate_decompositions.json entries as 11 transversals partitioning 121 cells and covering exactly the 363 seed set. Scope is exactly multiplier-isomorphism; broader isotopy explicitly excluded. No sampling; all searches exhaustive.

originality.rationale: Fused live retrieval (one scope_literature_search call with 3 normalized forms; SerpBase 10 + Crossref 15 per query ok, OpenAlex 0 hits, no partial failure) plus direct official-database fetches found no prior recording C=363, the 10-value per-seed spectrum, or a DCLS(11) mate table. Nearest priors: Wanless DB holds only two order-11 exemplars (LS11mosttrans 37851 provisional winner, LS11fewtrans 778 explicitly possibly-not-minimal); OEIS A003111/A006717 hold only raw totals 3441/37851 with stated transversal=orthomorphism=semi-queen equivalence; Wanless Diagonally cyclic latin squares (2004) defines the family/isomorphism notions (Introduction/Literature/Basic results/Orthogonality/MOLS based on Parker squares/Subsquare-free) with no order-11 census; Egan-Wanless enumerates MOLS/mates only to n<=9; Maenhaut-Wanless enumerates 7 atomic order-11 classes plus mates of cyclic squares only; Hulpke-Kaski-Ostergard counts all order-11 classes (~2e21 species) proving full census infeasible; Vatutin diagonal-Latin (DLS) families are a different family. Adversarial encodings checked (see decisive_checks); no broader theorem, census, or table substantively implies the per-seed distribution. Mate universality is elementary given the DCLS definition but no prior table states K=363 with per-seed decompositions, and it does not imply the spectrum.

value.rationale: TARGET audit against admitted target; no preset-fallback presumption applies. Result is an exact invariant table over a pre-motivated natural object: DCLS(11)/orthomorphisms of Z11 from the Hall-Paige through Wanless DCLS to Cavenagh-Hamalainen-Nelson program, at prime order 11 where full order-11 census (~1.22e25 isotopy classes) is infeasible so DCLS(11) is the literature-standard census unit, not an arbitrary slice. Gap predates computation (database held only 37851/778 exemplars; no seed-level distribution, no DCLS-maximum, no mate classification). Values were not known or mechanically implied: raw totals 3441/37851 do not imply C=363 or any per-seed count; group-square count does not imply maximality over DCLS(11). Future researchers can reasonably need the precise seed list, spectrum, maximum witness, and decomposition certificates for orthomorphism studies, rainbow-matching benchmarks, and mate-search pipelines at neighboring prime orders. This is an eligible narrow exact census datum under the value policy, not a textbook restatement, parameter substitution, tiny gain, or unexplained enumeration: every clause is machine-checked twice plus replay with archived witnesses and hashes.

broader_coverage.evidence: Fused queries 1 and 3 (literal DCLS(11) spectrum census; dominance query naming Egan-Wanless, Wanless DB 37851, Vatutin) returned Egan-Wanless (n<=9), Hulpke-Kaski-Ostergard order-11 total counts, Eberhard asymptotics, McKay-McLeod-Wanless bounds, Best-Wanless parity-type results, and Ollis-Tripp group-based complete squares. None tabulates transversals per DCLS(11) seed or classifies mates at order 11. Full order-11 census infeasibility motivates rather than covers the symmetry-subclass census.
broader_coverage.search: Dominance query: stronger theorem / broader object class / larger range / exhaustive census / database covering DCLS(11) as special case.
broader_coverage.why_not_cover: Broader counts (all order-11 species/isotopy classes) compute no transversal numbers and use a different equivalence; n<=9 mate censuses stop before order 11; asymptotic/parity/bound theorems do not imply any exact per-seed count.

claim_vs_prior_implication.evidence: Prior facts: 11*3441=37851 total; cyclic group square has 37851 transversals (Cavenagh-Wanless/A006717 comment; Wanless DB LS11mosttrans); broken diagonals give >=2n transversals. None implies the 363-class partition, the 10-value distribution, that non-linear seeds lie in 3333..4411, or that the 9 linear maps are the unique DCLS-maximizers. Mate universality M(i,j)=j-i follows elementarily from L_theta(i,j)=theta(j-i)+i for any theta, but no prior source was found stating K=363 with archived per-seed 11-way decompositions; in any case a mate corollary does not imply the transversal-count spectrum.
claim_vs_prior_implication.search: Tested whether any known stronger fact (totals, group-square count, general DCLS orthogonality) substantively implies or exhaustively covers the submitted headline.
claim_vs_prior_implication.why_not_cover: Totals and single-square counts underdetermine the distribution; maximum over R requires per-seed comparison, supplied here by two agreeing exhaustive counters plus replay; mate clause is separately certified per seed rather than inferred.

equivalent_formulations.evidence: Query 2 (orthomorphism Z11 / complete mapping / multiplier equivalence / Parker turn-square) fused to Evans orthomorphism-graph survey, Hsiang-Shieh-Hsu cyclic complete-mapping counting, OEIS equivalence comments (transversal of cyclic square = orthomorphism = semi-queen), and Wanless Parker-square terminology. Found only total-count equivalences (3441/37851), no per-orbit (C=363) or per-seed transversal table under any synonym.
equivalent_formulations.search: Synonymous names/notation and dual/complement/incidence/matrix encodings: orthomorphism, complete mapping, semi-queen, toroidal semi-queen, Parker square, turn-square, good permutation, transversals of cyclic group table.
equivalent_formulations.why_not_cover: Equivalences fix the raw universe size but not the multiplier-orbit classification or any per-seed transversal number; no source under an alternate name records the 363-seed spectrum.

Vatutin cyclic-diagonal/DLS rows (A338562/A341585/A348212 per admission) count a different family under restricted permutations and do not list 363 multiplier classes or this spectrum. exact_database_or_table.search: Exact parameter/object in tables or official databases: Wanless transversal DB order-11 files, OEIS A003111/A006717/A071607/A338562/A341585/A348212, Vatutin DLS lists.

residual_risks: Wanless (2004) PDF raw fetch returned binary without extractable text; coverage assessed via DOI metadata, section outline, secondary citations, and admission record - low risk that a hidden order-11 table exists, contradicted by database holding only two exemplars.
OpenAlex returned 0 hits on all three queries; SerpBase and Crossref succeeded with no partial failure flag - priority assessment rests on available providers plus direct official-database checks.
Mate universality proof is short and may be folklore; this affects only the mate clause's surprise, not the spectrum's novelty or the audit's correctness/value finding.

Correctness rests on exhaustive search code (stdlib Python) re-executed via replay; independent per-value recounts by auditor cover one seed per value, with full 363-value agreement via two independent counters plus replay third-method spots.
